title: How an Escalator Works in 60 Seconds 🪜⚙️ #shorts
description:
On every escalator, about half the steps are hidden, riding upside down underneath you. All the steps hang on a loop of chain pulled by a motor at the top, and each step rolls on two sets of wheels on two separate tracks. Where the tracks split apart, flat steps become stairs, and where they come back together, the stairs flatten into a moving floor. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#escalator #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: On every escalator, about *half the steps* are hidden, riding *upside down* underneath you.

steps.label: Chain
steps.text: All the steps hang on a giant loop of *chain*, pulled by a *motor* and gears at the top.

steps.label: Wheels
steps.text: Each step rolls on *two sets of wheels*, running on two separate tracks.

steps.label: Stairs
steps.text: On the slope, the tracks *split apart*. Each step stays level, so *stairs* appear.

steps.label: Flatten
steps.text: Near the ends, the tracks come back together, and the steps *flatten* into a moving floor.

steps.label: Handrail
steps.text: A *comb plate* guides your feet off, while a rubber *handrail* loops around at the same speed.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Loop, tracks, *stairs*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
